scope: Initial primary-source registry for the mechanisms research reset; not a systematic review.
local_snapshot_policy: Archive a permitted stable version and its SHA-256 before relying on detailed methods or theorem assumptions; do not fabricate missing snapshots.

sources.title: Reconciling modern machine-learning practice and the classical bias–variance trade-off
sources.relevance: Double-descent evidence is broader than deep neural networks; a risk curve needs an explicit model-complexity interpretation.
sources.limits: Not proof that every model or dataset must show a peak, or that all peaks share one cause.

sources.title: Surprises in High-Dimensional Ridgeless Least Squares Interpolation
sources.relevance: Analyzes minimum-norm least-squares interpolation for linear and nonlinear random-feature distributions.
sources.limits: Asymptotic and distributional assumptions must be checked in full text; not a theorem for arbitrary finite MLP or boosting.

sources.title: The generalization error of random features regression: Precise asymptotics and double descent curve
sources.relevance: Tractable random-features ridge model with a fixed random first layer motivates a controlled nonlinear comparison.
sources.limits: The analyzed high-dimensional sphere setting is not interchangeable with learned neural representations or real tabular data.

sources.title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
sources.relevance: Studies neural double descent with model size, training epochs and training-sample regimes.
sources.limits: Does not guarantee a peak on the historical Qwen embedding task or license mixing different axes in one curve.

sources.title: A U-turn on Double Descent: Rethinking Parameter Counting in Statistical Learning
sources.relevance: Challenges parameter-count interpretations of non-neural curves through distinct complexity axes and smoother-based effective parameters.
sources.limits: Its conclusions concern investigated setups; they are not a general impossibility theorem for single-axis GBDT double descent.

sources.title: Evaluating Double Descent in Machine Learning: Insights from Tree-Based Models Applied to a Genomic Prediction Task
sources.relevance: Reports joint-versus-separate learner-capacity and ensemble-size scaling in genomic and synthetic settings.
sources.limits: Preprint and limited tasks; not proof of universal absence of single-axis peaks. Exact definitions must be compared with L07.

sources.title: Double Descent in Gradient Boosting Decision Trees via Split-Candidate Scaling
sources.relevance: Proposes a split-candidate capacity intervention, tree-kernel diagnostics, and predictions for depth, sample size and label noise.
sources.limits: Preprint; a replication is a baseline rather than automatic novelty. Quantization and tree-kernel construction require full-text validation.

sources.title: Gradient Boosting Performs Gaussian Process Inference
sources.relevance: Connects a symmetric-tree boosting construction to a kernel method converging to a kernel-ridge solution.
sources.limits: No blanket Gaussian-process equivalence for the repository's arbitrary CatBoost Logloss setup; check loss, randomization and convergence assumptions.
